fixes.explanation: Not this time, baker. The verse says the LORD “…spared His people.” and scattering them isn't anywhere in it. Joel 2:18 has the LORD become jealous for His land, and then He spares. I think that's a very good turn for a verse to take.

Yes, baker, Western is the word. Joel 2:20 says the front ranks go “…into the Eastern Sea, and its rear guard into the Western Sea.” The front ranks go to one sea and the rear guard goes to the other.

Fair guess, baker, since that's a sea people know. But Joel 2:20 doesn't use that name. It says the front ranks go into the Eastern Sea and the rear guard into the Western Sea. I read recipes like that too, hunting for a fancy name when the card just says left or right.

That's a creative one, friend, but silent isn't what the verse says. Joel 2:22 says, “…for the open pastures have turned green…” It's a color, and it's the good kind. Silent is how my bakery gets when a batch burns, and that has never made anybody less afraid. Green pastures do.
That's the opposite of the verse, baker. Joel 2:24 says the threshing floors “…will be full of grain…” Empty isn't in the promise at all. Full is.

No, friend, it's the other direction. In Joel 2:25 God says, “I will repay you for the years eaten by locusts…” Nothing in the verse counts them against anyone. It's God promising to repay, and that's good news for the people.

Not what the text says, baker. In Joel 2:25 God is the one speaking, and He ends with “…My great army that I sent against you.” He is the one who says He sent them. Enemies aren't named as the senders here.
That's not in the verse, friend. The text doesn't mention fathers or a curse here. In Joel 2:25 God says, “…My great army that I sent against you.” God calls them His army, not a curse.

That's the big finish, baker. In Joel 2:27 God says, “Then you will know that I am present in Israel and that I am the LORD your God, and there is no other.” After everything He does, this is what they'll know. I think that's better than any harvest.

Good thought, baker, but the verse doesn't promise that. In Joel 2:27 God says, “Then you will know that I am present in Israel…” The thing they'll know is about God being present, not about the harvest.

Understandable guess, friend, but the verse doesn't say it. In Joel 2:27 God says, “Then you will know that I am present in Israel and that I am the LORD your God, and there is no other.” What they'll know is about Him.
True, baker. In Joel 2:27 God says, “…I am the LORD your God, and there is no other.” He says it plainly, in His own words.
